To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oral bioavailability of atorvastain (ATV) in rats is low because of extensive hepatic and intestinal extraction and metabolism, and that rifampicin markedly increased the plasma levels of ATV and its hydroxy metabolites by inhibition of hepatic uptake and intestinal extraction.

1) ATV and its metabolite undergo extensive hepatic metabolism in vivo, 2) hepatic Oatps contribute significantly to the hepatic metabolism of ATV and its hydroxy metabolite, and 3) RIF reduces the hepatic metabolic extraction of ATV and its 3'-hydroxy and 4'-hydroxy metabolites by inhibiting the hepatic Oatp-mediated transport of ATV.
the oral bioavailability of atorvastain is low in rats because of extensive metabolism in the gut and liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a rat model to study hepatic drug elimination.
the role of hepatic uptake and metabolism in the pharmacokinetics of ATV and its hydroxy metabolites in rats, and the effect of coadministration of RIF on these processes.
the pharmacokinetics of ATV and its hydroxy metabolites in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RIF inhibits the uptake transporters Oatps, and this leads to increased plasma levels of ATV, its metabolites, and the metabolite-to-parent AUC ratio.
RIF, a strong inhibitor of hepatic Oatps, significantly increased the plasma concentrations and AUC0-∝ of ATV and its two metabolites in rats.
RIF, a potent inhibitor of Oatps, significantly increased the systemic exposure of ATV and its hydroxy metabolites, which may be clinically relevant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Oatps are important in the elimination of ATV in rats, and that Oatp-mediated hepatic uptake is the major determinant of hepatic extraction and first-pass metabolism of ATV.
hepatic Oatps play a key role in the elimination of ATV in rats, but intestinal metabolism and gut uptake are also significant contributors.
the first-pass effect from both intestinal and hepatic metabolism and the hepatic first-pass effect from Oatp-mediated hepatic elimination are important factors in the disposition of ATV in rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the first-pass effect of ATV in rats is not solely dependent on hepatic metabolism but is a combination of hepatic and gut metabolism.
the hepatic elimination of ATV and metabolites in rats is mediated primarily by Oatp-mediated hepatic uptake.

the hepatic uptake of drugs by Oatp is an important determinant of hepatic drug elimination and that it is important to consider the role of Oatp-mediated hepatic uptake in the development of new drugs and the design of drug-drug interaction studies.
